newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Next Media mulls legal action vs SHK Intl. [CORRECTED 06:01 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Next Media mulls legal action vs SHK Intl. [CORRECTED 06:01 GMT]

text.p: Hong Kong publisher Next Media Group Ltd, founded by flamboyant garment king Jimmy Lai, said on Friday it planned to take legal action against Sun Hung Kai International Ltd for withdrawing as underwriter of Next's IPO.
"We have decided to take legal action against SHK for compensation of losses due to the delay," Yeung Wai-hong, group chairman of Next Media, told a news conference.
Yeung said SHK International informed Next Media on Thursday it had formally withdrawn as sponsor of the proposed listing (corrects when Next Media was informed).
SHK International managing director Peter Fung has said the underwriter faced pressure over the issue, Yeung said.
SHK International officials were not immediately available for comment.
"Up to now we still don't know what the reasons are and what difficulties he (Fung) encountered," Yeung said.
"In the past three years, the group has been in contact with a total of 12 merchant banks for the listing. One of them told the group it could not help because of political problems."
Lai, who founded the magazine known for its robust views on China and which has frequently angered the authorities in Beijing, holds 80 percent of the group's shares.
The listing would have diluted his holding to about 60 percent.
Lai's most famous written attack was directed at Chinese Premier Li Peng in 1994.
Chinese authorities have responded by barring reporters from Next group publications, as well as those working for Lai's newspaper, Apple Daily, from covering events in China.
Yeung said SHK International had informed the company verbally of its decision but not in writing.
"We won't abandon our listing plan," he said.
Yeung said the company would consider exploring other markets outside Hong Kong though it would prefer to list in the territory.
"There are a lot of markets," he added, "but our first option is Hong Kong."
